title: Australia unemployment rate July 2026
question: What will the Australian Bureau of Statistics report as Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for July 2026 in Labour Force, Australia, first print?
resolutionSource: Australian Bureau of Statistics Labour Force, Australia, July 2026
resolutionRule: Resolve to the national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (%) for Australia in ABS Labour Force, Australia, July 2026, first published on 20/08/2026 at 11:30am AEST. Use the first-print value as ABS prints it, normally to one decimal percent, and ignore later revisions or later corrected reposts.
drivers: Latest ABS first-print anchor is May 2026 seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of 4.4%.
Trend unemployment rate has edged up to 4.4%, keeping the underlying level above early-2026 readings.
May reversed part of April's spike, so persistence should not extrapolate April's 4.5% mechanically.
Two unreleased monthly prints remain before July, so sampling volatility is material.

reasoning.text: Framing and exact resolver: this is the ABS Labour Force, Australia national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for July 2026, first print. The ledger table label says June 2026, but the dataPointId and question target July 2026; I keep the target tied to July 2026 and resolve from the July 2026 ABS release.

reasoning.result: Fetched future releases: June 2026 releases 23/07/2026 11:30am AEST; July 2026 releases 20/08/2026 11:30am AEST; August 2026 releases 24/09/2026 11:30am AEST.

reasoning.call: ABS Labour Force, Australia latest release key statistics for May 2026
reasoning.result: Fetched May 2026 seasonally adjusted unemployment rate 4.4%, April 2026 4.5%, unemployed people 671,300 in May, employment 14,738,800 in May, participation rate 66.7%.

reasoning.result: Fetched same-variant unrounded seasonally adjusted unemployment rates: Jan-26 4.082555, Feb-26 4.301710, Mar-26 4.278411, Apr-26 4.481340, May-26 4.355949; trend rates Mar-26 4.327248, Apr-26 4.348103, May-26 4.361273.
Fetched July 2026 collection timing: Jul-26 reference week starts 28 June 2026 and ends 11 July 2026; enumeration starts 5 July 2026 and ends 25 July 2026.

reasoning.text: Variant control: all anchors and dispersion inputs are the ABS national seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for Australia, not trend, original, state, or sex-specific rates; trend is used only as a directional current-condition cross-check.

The reference class and base rate are recent monthly moves in the same ABS seasonally adjusted unemployment-rate series. From Jul-23 through May-26, the rate rose from 3.697010 to 4.355949, but individual monthly changes were noisy, including Apr-26 up to 4.481340 and May-26 down to 4.355949.

Level and momentum: May's 4.355949 is the cleanest public anchor. The trend estimate of 4.361273 and year-on-year unemployment-rate increase of 0.3 percentage points argue for a level around 4.4 to 4.5 rather than a reversion to early-2026 levels near 4.1.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior from May-26 seasonally adjusted 4.355949, historical sample Jul-23 to May-26 same-series monthly changes, adjustment components +0.05 for two months of trend drift and +0.05 for weaker year-on-year labour-market slack, interval method based on monthly successive-change dispersion where monthly sigma is 0.146 percentage points and two-month sigma = sqrt(2)*0.146 = 0.206; using sigma = 0.206 gives 1.28*sigma = 0.264, giving final implied bounds around 4.2 to 4.7 after first-print rounding.

Point calculation: 4.355949 May anchor + 0.05 trend drift + 0.05 slack adjustment = 4.455949, rounded to a one-decimal first-print forecast of 4.5%. Interval calculation: center about 4.46 with half-width about 0.26 gives 4.19 to 4.72, reported as ciLow 4.2 and ciHigh 4.7.

Counter-considerations: upside risk is a June or July employment loss with participation holding near 66.7%, which would land above the interval. Downside risk is another May-like fall in unemployed people plus lower participation, which would land below the interval. A one-off rotation-group or survey-modernisation effect outside normal sampling variability could also push the first print outside the interval.

Review disposition: accepted the blocking coherence critique by revising the stated adjustment arithmetic so the unrounded forecast supports a 4.5% one-decimal first-print point estimate; also accepted the interval clarification by using a two-month sigma derived from the monthly-change dispersion. Kept the ledger table-label discrepancy note because it preserves the July 2026 target while flagging the apparent June-label issue.
